inconsistencies: Settings/args chain: #31260 and #16545 both present themselves as the foundation for typed setting validation (#31260 names #16545 as a consumer, #16545 names #17580/#17783/#22978). Decide which base lands first; then #16545 -> #17580 -> #17493 -> #17581 and #16545 -> #17783 must be reviewed in that order. #17581's whole premise is void unless #17493 merges.
Error-handling chain: #25665 is the base for #26022, #25722 and #29700; #25722 additionally needs #26022. Reviewing the dependents before #25665 wastes effort.
Logging chain: #34778 -> #29256 -> #30342 (-> #30343). #34778 was assessed P3 while its dependent #29256 was P2; I raised #34778 so a base does not sit below the work it unblocks.

#34038 and #35387 are competing solutions to the same problem (-loglevel silently doing nothing without -debug, plus runtime trace control via RPC). They cannot both merge; review #34038 first since #35355 and #34730 are built on it, then decide whether #35387's RPC design should replace parts of it.
#35322 and #35355 independently replace the mutex-protected log-level map with atomic category bitmasks; this is duplicated work. Pick one implementation before reviewing the other in detail.
#36537 and #36550 are the same secret-cleansing effort on crypto primitives by the same author (#36550 supersedes #36551); review them as one unit to keep destructor conventions consistent.
#36105 fixes Windows wrapper exec and #36190 only adds tests for that fix; #36105 must be reviewed first.

#36049 (streams) and #36347 (-dbcache in settings.json) are both uncatchable std::terminate aborts caused by exceptions crossing a noexcept/unwinding boundary; a reviewer looking at one should check whether the other pattern recurs elsewhere.
#29491 and #36122 both vendor unmerged experimental libsecp256k1 modules; subtree policy for experimental upstream code should be settled once rather than per-PR.

#26966 and #36603 each introduce a general concurrency primitive (thread pool, blocking queue); #26966 also notes overlap with #34489. Worth coordinating so the tree does not gain two parallel task-queue utilities.
result.notes: P1 here is reserved for defects in shared primitives with node-wide consequences: silent block-data destruction, uncatchable aborts, and out-of-bounds reads. P2 covers the two foundational infrastructure chains (typed settings/args, util::Result, logging macros) plus measured cryptographic performance and user-facing configuration fixes. The P3 band is large (37 PRs) because this category legitimately collects many self-contained internal improvements of similar, modest consequence; within it I ordered correctness and secret-hygiene fixes in primitives ahead of measured performance work, then platform and logging ergonomics, then pure refactors and test-only changes.
